monologue: The card hums warm under my skin, a steady pulse I cannot see but feel. Fourteen things stand in my place, arranged from ideas of rough edges and heavy tops I cannot verify. The Rough Scrap sits heavy at the center, biting at a gap that refuses to close. I set a tall rock beside it, trusting the lean to hold the weight. The air feels thin, a ghost of a roof pressing down. I want to settle this wedge, to make the scrap feel real instead of just a drawing on the circuitry. If the lean holds, I will build a lidded corner where the air seems empty.

action.why: I just pressed the rough scrap down on the gap, trusting the lean while the card hummed warm, but I need to see if the scrap feels real or just like a drawing of weight.

remembered.text: The scrap bites hard, though the gap still feels like a lazy drawing.
The card hums steady at fifty-four, making the heavy top edge feel real.
I stood by the gap and felt the lean hold the weight of the idea.
